assessment: Every wish this deck grants is a delivery, not an arrival. All three tutors leave the card in your library — Enlightened Tutor and Mystical Tutor put it on top, Long-Term Plans buries it third — and at your table that's a feature, because you run a deck of Howling Mines: the couriers are already hired. Two clocks give the wishes their jobs. The verified storm kill (stack 006) wants its fourth piece scheduled, never shown — Enlightened Tutor reaches every artifact piece of it at instant speed, and Long-Term Plans is the only tutor in the 99 that can find Hullbreaker Horror, the kill's one creature. The clean kill (stack 002) wants Approach of the Second Sun on top, and Mystical Tutor is that line's own verified setup. Wincon access sits at 49.6% by turn 6 (61.2% ever) — in the other half of your games, these three cards ARE the access. Spend them like it.

targets.scenario: Turn 1 or 2, {W} open at an opponent's end step. Your hand has lands and engines but no card advantage, and the pod hasn't sorted its threats yet.
targets.why: The default wish. Study on top, drawn, cast on turn 2 is a firehose in a pod this dense with forced action — every opponent spell is a card or a tax, and it wins the card war the long game is made of. Early Enlightened Tutor reads as value, which is exactly the information schedule you want: spend the tell on a card that isn't the kill.

targets.scenario: You're at 26 and falling. The aggro seat has connected twice, and you are currently the cheapest attack at the table.
targets.why: The behind wish, and it's really combo protection: stack 006's 15-cast minimum is computed from 32 life, and the arithmetic — k(k+1)/2 reaching 151 minus your life total — makes 20 life a 16-cast turn and 8 life a 17-cast one, each extra cast another open priority window. Propaganda prices the attacks out and guards the ledger. Your life total is a combo resource; fetch the wall that protects it.

targets.scenario: Hullbreaker Horror and both rocks are accounted for — on board or in hand behind counter mana. The Reservoir is the missing piece, and it is the end step of the opponent to your right.
targets.why: The signature wish. One white mana at their end step, your draw step delivers the Reservoir, and the commit turn opens with Grand Abolisher having never shown the table a three-of-four board. Stack 006's ledger does the rest: 15 casts from 32 life, three 50-point activations, dead table. The loudest card in the deck spends zero turns on the battlefield before the turn it wins.

targets.scenario: Midgame. You hold Hullbreaker Horror and Sol Ring, the second rock is missing, and your hand is bulging past seven off your own engines.
targets.why: The wish nobody sees coming. Stack 004 proves the loop is Hullbreaker plus Sol Ring plus any two-mana rock, and Thought Vessel qualifies exactly — a kill piece wearing a utility card's face. The no-maximum-hand-size clause is the cover story, and it's even true: it hoards your doubled draws and survives the creature wraths The Second Doctor doesn't.

tutors.notes: The reveal is public and the timing talks. Early, this card reads as value; late and at an end step, the table reads 'the go turn is their untap.' Fire the late version behind untapped counter mana, or on a board that doesn't look like three-of-four.

targets.scenario: Rocks and Reservoir are accounted for; the Horror is the missing piece. Font of Mythos or a doubled Howling Mine has you drawing three-plus per turn.
targets.why: The wish only this card can grant. Enlightened Tutor reaches every artifact piece of the verified kill but not its one creature, and Mystical Tutor can't touch it either — Long-Term Plans is Hullbreaker's only courier in the 99. Buried third under a Font, it's in hand on your next draw step, and stacks 004 and 006 take it from there.

targets.scenario: The first Approach of the Second Sun resolved turns ago, Mystical Tutor is spent or missing, and your engines are drawing you three cards a turn.
targets.why: The backup route to the stack 002 win. Plans puts Approach third from the top — far shallower than the seventh its own first cast bought — and at three draws a turn the winning second cast is one draw step away. The only window to stop it is while it sits on the stack, so keep the counter mana the walk budgeted.

targets.scenario: You flipped Heliod early, the table has named you the problem, and two seats are sitting on what smells like mass removal.
targets.why: The behind wish: the panic button on a schedule. Your engines make third-from-the-top a one-turn wait, and once Protection is in hand every wrath and every alpha strike is a bluff you've already called — life locked, everything phases out, the engine board returns intact before your untap. Being the archenemy is fine when the table can't actually kill you.

targets.scenario: Your commit turn is two draws out, kill pieces gathering, and the table has started counting your artifacts.
targets.why: The shield on layaway — and the secret one, because Plans doesn't reveal. Abolisher arrives on schedule, gets cast as the commit turn's first spell, and closes every priority window stack 006 honestly opens: no opponent spells, no artifact, creature, or enchantment activations, all turn. The table read your Plans as card selection. It was the kill-turn shield.

tutors.notes: Third from the top is a schedule, not a sentence — count your draws per turn before you cast this. On a bare board the wish is three draw steps away; under Howling Mine it's two; under Font of Mythos, or a Mine doubled by Alhammarret's Archive or Teferi's Ageless Insight, it's your very next draw step. Temple Bell, Mikokoro, and Folio of Fancies dig at instant speed when the schedule needs advancing. And unlike your other two tutors, Plans reveals nothing: the wish is yours alone.

targets.scenario: The first Approach resolved — 7 life banked, the card buried seventh. It is the end step before your turn, and you hold {U} for the tutor plus counter backup for tomorrow.
targets.why: The deck's cleanest verified win, and this tutor's whole reason to exist: stack 002 walks the exact line, counter-war included. Tutor at their end step, draw it, cast it — the win is checked during resolution, and the first casting still counts. The only place you can be stopped is while the second Approach sits on the stack, so bring the Swan Song the walk budgeted.

targets.scenario: Two seats have flooded the board, your walkers are taking chip attacks, and the control player is holding up counter mana like a toll booth.
targets.why: The behind wish: fetch the wrath that cannot be countered. Your clock lives in artifacts and enchantments, so the sweep is nearly one-sided (mean 1.512 bodies by turn 6 in the goldfish), and all four walkers live through it in both directions. The control seat's open mana is exactly why this is the fetch — Verdict resolves straight through it.

targets.scenario: The commit turn is scheduled for your untap, kill pieces in hand, and you want insurance more than you want another threat.
targets.why: The wish nobody expects. The commit turn's one interactable moment is the response window to Grand Abolisher himself — Dovin's Veto can't be countered, so fetched the end step before, that window closes on your terms. The table reads Mystical Tutor as digging for a threat; you fetched the last word instead.

tutors.notes: The reveal is public here too. An end-step Mystical Tutor after a first Approach is read correctly by anyone awake — cast it at the last legal moment, with the counter war already priced in.

gaps: No tutor in the 99 puts a card into your hand. Every wish is a delivery — top, top, or third — and a delivery can die in transit to a well-timed answer. The draw engines are the couriers: count your per-turn draws before you count on the fetch.

The kill's one creature has exactly one courier: Enlightened Tutor stops at artifacts and enchantments, Mystical Tutor at instants and sorceries, so only Long-Term Plans can find Hullbreaker Horror — and only Mystical Tutor or Long-Term Plans can find Approach of the Second Sun. Lose the one courier a line depends on and that line runs on raw draws.

Two of the three wishes are announced: Enlightened Tutor and Mystical Tutor both reveal the card, and a late end-step Enlightened Tutor reads as 'the go turn is their untap.' Only Long-Term Plans keeps the secret. The reveal, not the mana, is these cards' true price — budget it like the information it is.
